nodes.label: IBM Plex Sans Typeface
nodes.rationale: Weight 300 is used for display sizes (42-76px) deliberately - it reads as quietly authoritative and differentiates IBM from competing enterprise brands that use bold 700-weight display type; the font is also free/open-source (SIL OFL) which makes it the easiest custom face on the list to substitute in implementation.

nodes.label: IBM Blue Single Accent Color
nodes.rationale: IBM Blue (#0f62fe) is treated as a scarce resource - the single chromatic brand accent reserved for links, primary CTAs, focus underlines, and the CTA banner - to keep visual hierarchy disciplined and avoid introducing a second brand color that would dilute the enterprise-gravitas voice.

nodes.label: Flat Square-Corner Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Every CTA, card, input, and container commits to 0px corner radius and 1px hairline borders instead of shadows, because rounded corners or drop shadows would make the brand read as a generic stylized SaaS product rather than engineered, old-world enterprise gravitas reframed for the cloud era.

nodes.label: 4px Base Spacing Grid
nodes.rationale: All spacing tokens (4px-96px) are multiples of a 4px base unit so alignment stays predictable and precise across breakpoints - Carbon's signature grid discipline replaces large atmospheric whitespace with dense, precisely-aligned content.

nodes.label: Host Networking Mode Decision
nodes.rationale: The app needs to reach devices (MikroTik routers, etc.) on the LAN, which the isolated postgres_default bridge network has no route to, so the container uses network_mode: host to bind straight to the host's network stack and reach LAN devices directly, at the cost of ports:/networks: no longer applying and DB_HOST needing to be reachable from the host itself.

nodes.label: Jump-Host Remote Access Model
nodes.rationale: All remote access (VNC/RDP/SSH) must route through a controlled jump host/proxy rather than connecting the frontend directly to target devices, so that credentials are never exposed to the frontend, every session is logged and auditable, and access can be centrally revoked - required for patient-safety and compliance/auditability constraints in a hospital environment.
